_: What's new fragments already stamped with the build they went live in, folded here by tools/config/foldChangelog.mjs under their old file names (the docs tidy, Ed 2026-11-15). Don't edit by hand: add a new fragment file instead (CLAUDE.md, What's new).

items: Every kind of wood now grows its own mix of three to six kinds of tree, in its own shades
Ten new trees: wild cherry in blossom, crab apple, elder, aspen, silvery whitebeam, field elm and flat-tiered cedar

Three magical ones, rarely and only where magic suits: glowing mushroom trees in the hazel rings, crystal-leaf trees by the cave mouth, and vine-hung trees with glowing buds in the old garden and the holly thicket

Try the new pixel-art looks while playing: add ?style=bold (bold flat tones with coloured outlines) or ?style=ref (the boar reference's look, with strong dark outlines), and ?px=4 or ?px=5 for bigger art pixels. Without them the game looks as it did

Animals talk when they attack: a burst of babble in their own voice, squeaky for small young ones and rumbling for big adults and legends; happy ones chirp, enraged ones snap and snarl, wild ones grumble
Creatures turning angry or happy say so in their own voice
Your 💌s will be your witch chattering away, each burst a little phrase lifting at the end, as soon as they land
Evolving now costs 2 berries then 2 (was 1 then 3): still 4 from baby to adult, each berry buying the same strength. Berry patches are bigger, so there are more berries about
Areas are bigger (about half as wide again, 168 m across) and fewer (14 by 14), so the forest is about the same size but each area has more room

Every area has room to fight round its middle and its soundsystem: mostly open ground, the woods thickening gradually out to the area's normal forest, with lone trees and bushes thinning into the clearing
Berry bushes and berries are as thick on the ground as before in the bigger areas
The ring round a party animal is split into one segment for each berry it needs; each berry it eats lights a segment, and the ones still to eat show pale

The dodge (W) is now a blink: she vanishes and reappears 10 m on the way she's going (or facing, if she's still), with a puff of motes where she left, a burst where she lands and a faint streak between
She can't be hit in the instant she's gone, and she never lands inside a tree, a rock, a soundsystem or the treehouse: the blink stops short at the last clear spot
The legendary boar charges head down with enormous twisting horns sweeping back over its hump, fire at their tips, its eyes glinting below; the adult shows their first nubs
Bushes, ferns and grass tufts are drawn the same way as the trees now: leafy domes lit from one side, flowering shrubs with clusters of blossom, ferns as a fan of fronds, grass in leaning clumps
?style=bold and ?style=ref now give the bushes the pixel-art look too

The oaks, beeches, ashes, limes and the other broadleaf trees now have crowns built from the same leaf stamps as the rest of the forest: each clump lit from one side and dark beneath, swaying on its own in the wind
The sprigs and low boughs on every tree's trunk are drawn the same way
Character creator: the sliders go much further, for huge hats, tiny brims, giant brooms
Every colour has a rainbow picker: 256 hues, a shade and a grey strip
New: no hat, a hat picker, scarf length, bag size and backpack size (the new hats and bags are still being drawn)
🌀 Wild: a witch with everything anywhere

The character creator is now her messy treehouse bedroom, seen from above: the bed with her laptop glowing on it, clothes and hats everywhere, open books with glowing runes, DJ decks, a guitar, a synth and a drum, potions and crystals, candles, the PARTY TONIGHT banner, and a round window on the night
Click her to switch between standing and hovering on her broom

Make your own witch while the forest grows: the game opens in her treehouse room (a mirror, and a banner: PARTY TONIGHT) and you dress her up: hat (shape, height, lean, brim), hair, top and cloak, broom, accessories and the colour of every part, with Randomise and Classic buttons
Start shows how far the forest has grown; press it early and she's "getting ready" until it's done, then straight into play
She's remembered on this browser for next time
Every look keeps her a witch: always a pointed hat with its glowing band, and a broom

Creatures pull faces: an enraged one glares with its brows down, a party animal (or a friendly area's creature) beams with its eyes closed in smiling arcs, and a stunned one looks dazed with crossed-out or odd eyes
The faces are part of each creature, not marks over its head, and each family has its own: feathery brows on birds and bats, brow ridges on snakes and beetles

Animals now have four moods. Wild: as they were. Happy: invited, they stay in their own area, defend it against sieges and dance at its soundsystem. Leashed: invited a second time, they're yours for good. Enraged: offended by a new soundsystem in their area, they besiege the nearest one
Wild and happy animals leave each other alone, and so do wild and enraged; your leashed animals take on the wild and the enraged; the enraged go for the happy; still nobody fights its own kind
Nobody is killed: a knocked-down wild animal lies dazed for a while (you can still invite it), then runs off home; any other knocked down just runs off
Knocked down yourself, your carried sigils are put down where your animals stand, so they stay yours as a parked group
Until the 💌 invites arrive, chatting works the same way: one chat makes an animal happy, a second one leashes it
The boar evolves: a striped piglet, a heavy-fronted adult with a shoulder hump, a mane and curving tusks, and a massive legend with huge curling tusks, flame wisps and a shaggy mane
Creatures have fur, feathers, scales, plates, shells and bristles shaping their light (add ?texture=0 to compare)
A legend's dream bubble stacks the creature it wants above its face, and stays on screen when you stand close
Creatures far from you and from any fight are simulated less often (frozen far away), so late runs with hundreds of creatures cost less each frame
The debug overlay updates four times a second, its trees/bushes/creatures line no longer hidden under the buttons, and a new sim line counts creatures in full, coarse and frozen
Home's meadow is alive with sound: birdsong, bees and a breeze, fading out at home's edge

Ready for what's coming: a thump and whoosh when your witch is knocked back (and a dizzy twinkle while she's stunned), a charging legend's bellow, thundering hooves, rumble and skid, and a magical chime when you find a relic bottle

Smoother late runs: far less memory churned each frame (fewer sudden hitches), work done ahead now leaves room for the drawing, and party decorations, berries and the forest's look-ahead skip what's out of view or already done
The view glides instead of stepping a whole art pixel at a time when you move (add ?subpixel=0 to the link to compare with before)
The debug panel (~) shows what the frames really are: the frame time's spread, the slowest frames, and how long the game's own work and the GPU take each frame (where the browser can time it)

Esc (or Start on a gamepad, or the ❚❚ button by the volume) pauses everything, music too, as a still picture for screenshots; a panel shows the version, seed, game time, where you are, the area and the camera, with a link to copy; while paused, . steps one frame and Shift+. ten; Esc again carries on
A gentler start: every wild area begins with just a baby and a young one, so you can invite one and still leave its legend a creature of its own kind
The home speakers now take five minutes to boot up, counted from when you get up from the decks: no waves and no new creatures till then, and a note by the wave bar tells you when they're up
The witch's light is brighter right around her and falls away to dark much closer, so the forest round her has more depth

The ground in every area is grown by a new ground generator: moss in lit domes on the moor, pine needles and twigs, mud with little puddles, pebbles and slabs on the stony ground, fallen leaves, grass tufts, heather and bluebells, each in its area's own colours
With ?style=bold or ?style=ref the ground gets the pixel-art look too
The screen shakes when the witch is hit: a jolt on the first hit, harder on the next, and a big thump when she's knocked down. Turn it off on the start screen (screen shake on / off) or with ?shake=0
Home's area is now a whole circle round the dancefloor reaching past the treehouse, so no neighbouring area cuts into it; the areas round it are shaped round it
Home is a meadow of its own: fresh green grass and wildflowers, no trees
Party decorations are scattered all over home instead: lanterns, balloons, chairs, tables, flower pots, stepping stones and more
At the start the ley line leaves from the front of the treehouse, heading south towards you, then curves round to the first stone
Your 💌 invites now go one envelope at a time, tumbling end over end in a gentle lob that lands with a puff
They fly half as far again and a fifth faster; each creature needs a few more of them, so winning one over takes about as long as before

Invite with 💌s instead of chatting: on the ground, click (or hold 1) to throw a burst of spinning 💌s at the cursor; on a gamepad, aim with the right stick and throw with a trigger; on touch, the 💌 button throws them the way you're going
Each 💌 that lands fills a little meter of hearts over the creature (babies need a few, adults many); it drains slowly if you stop; full, the creature joins your party
A creature can only take one 💌's worth of affection every half second: a burst helps you invite a crowd, not one creature faster (the extra letters still land with a little ✨)
You call out with an emoji every time you throw, and the creature you hit answers, warming up as its meter fills
A creature's reply bubble is sized by its level: babies' smallest, legends' largest (yours stays the same)
Enraged creatures and legends block 💌s (they answer 😠); your own party animals let them through

Enraged creatures are tinted a soft red (easy to pick out, even from the treetops), wear angry brows over their red eyes and have a 💢 popping beside their heads; dazed ones see stars; happy ones wear party clothes without the glowing collar (that's for your party), and dance where there's a soundsystem; legends never dress up
Party animals, happy ones and your own, twinkle with a few little sparkles, so you can spot them in a crowd

A blow now throws you back and staggers you for a moment (you wobble, with stars round your hat, and can't move, blink or throw 💌s): a bite or a shot nudges you a couple of metres, a heavy blow further, and a charging boar or stag sends you flying about 12 m

A throw carries you straight through trees and bushes (you never end up inside one), a blink still dodges everything, and after a stagger you can't be staggered again for a second, so a pack can't keep you dazed
?knock=0 in the link turns the knockback off

Legend buffs redesigned: 30 different buffs, each changing only your 💌s (fans, rings, echoes, homing, piercing, ricochets, splitting, boomerangs, lantern trails, caches, orbiting 💌s...) or how you move (blink charges, longer blinks, speed after a blink...)
A 💌 is never stronger: buffs give more of them or change how they fly, and each animal still takes at most one every half second
Firing slows you a little on the ground (Ram's Steady takes that away)

Charging legends (boar, elk, stag, ram, hedgehog, woodlouse) charge across the map: head down with their lane shown on the ground, then a heavy run that curves after you, trampling everything in the way and knocking you aside, then a wide braking arc and the long walk home before they can charge again
Legends fight only with their long-range attacks for now
A legend's long-range lob and beam now have their own effects art: a target circle, the stone in flight and its slam ring, and the long beam
Lobbed shots land with a thud, a legend's with a deep boom
Legends sleep on through the party: a soundsystem no longer wakes them
Bring a sleeping legend the creature it dreams of before its area's soundsystem switches on, and its buff is yours for good; it sleeps on

Take every one of a legend's own kind out of its area and it grows restless, its dream turning to a nightmare; bring one back to calm it, or after a minute it wakes angry and lobs or beams at you and your posse from far off (never at soundsystems)

Giant party relics lie half buried about the forest: pick one up (it joins your stack, sigil button) and put it down by a sleeping legend to make it happy: its buff is yours, and it shoots the enraged from afar to defend you
A legend worn down goes back to sleep, and a buff you've earned from it is never taken away
The ley line now runs on through the next three runestones and back through the last three you reached
Only the next runestone has an on-screen marker

Losing a soundsystem brings the next wave a minute sooner (at once if less than a minute is left); each loss counts, and the waves after it keep their usual gap. The wave bar shrinks with a red flash and shows "−60 s"
When losing a soundsystem brings the next wave at once, its sting's clock races faster
Charging boars have weight: they lower their head, build up speed, thunder on past you, then skid round in a wide arc before coming again
Creatures in a fight speed up, slow down and turn smoothly, without jerking or flickering left and right; a momentum knob joins fight scale and speed in the debug panel (, and .)
Wild creatures give up the chase soon after you leave their area (about 10 m past its edge) and head back home
Animals don't bunch up any more: walking, following you, marching or fighting, each keeps some room round it, more for big ones (a bear keeps much more space than a dormouse)
The music no longer seems to stop when you fly away from home: far from the speakers it's quieter and muffled, but you can still hear it
A legend's nightmare shows one face that grows from slightly sad, through sadder and upset, to angry as it gets more restless

A sleeping legend's dream now shows only when you're on the ground near it, with a soft glow on its side pointing to the nearest runestone of the kind of area it dreams of; once its area's soundsystem is on, the dream is gone
A restless legend's dream turns to a nightmare, the creature it wants fading out; it tosses and turns in its sleep
Speech and dream bubbles share one pixel style and grow with the creature: babies smallest, legends largest
Party animals wear little party shoes: trainers, glitter, platforms, heels, boots or light-up trainers glowing in their neon, fitted to hooves, paws and claws, stepping with their legs
Home has picnics: blankets in gingham, stripes and tartan with baskets, cups, cakes and fruit on them, and picnic tables with benches or chairs round them
Taller balloons: single balloons and bunches high on long strings, bobbing in the breeze
Leaves now sway in clumps, each bunch moving a whole step at a time, instead of smearing
Treetop flight is half as fast again (48 m/s, from 32), and the treetop camera sits further out to match: Ed's pick from the playtest presets (168 m areas with 48 m/s)
Try bigger areas and faster treetop flight: add ?areaSize=280&treetopSpeed=96 to the link (remembered on this browser); treetop speed also has a slider in the debug panel (~), with a reset
Over the treetops the camera zooms out as treetop speed goes up, so the screen shows about the same few seconds of flight

The clearing round each runestone is smaller and its edge much softer: the woods thin gradually all the way from the area's edge towards the stone, and small things (ferns, flowers, grass) still grow in the middle

Sigils only go down and come up on the ground. In the treetops E (X on a gamepad, the sigil button on a phone) cycles them instead, the bottom one to the top, and its slot on the bar shows ↻; the separate cycle button (R) is gone
Try ?props=gen: the moor's standing stones are grey slabs, its cairns low heaps, its pools all different shapes, and the muddy forest's broken trunks keep their branches attached
Creatures on the ground now move with live animation: legs stepping on the ground, bodies leaning into turns and charges, crouching before a leap (add ?rig=0 to the address to see the old frames)
Legends always animate, even seen from the treetops
Party animals animate too, in their party gear, and enraged creatures keep their red eyes and red tint
Creatures' legs read as smooth limbs rather than strings of beads

A mixing pass on the sound: creatures' voices, her "ouch!", being knocked back, a soundsystem lost and a legend's charge are easier to hear over the music; home's meadow a little fuller; a relic's chime and her knockdown cry a touch softer
A 💌 that misses lands on the ground with a soft puff
When home's boot-up ends, the forest stirs: a low swell and far bells waking
Home's meadow has its balloons squeaking in the breeze and a picnic's cups clinking and far-off murmur
Losing a soundsystem is heard anywhere: the party grinds to a halt like a record stopping, then a little clock ticks faster as the next wave hurries closer
A legend winding up its slow long-range attack swells in its whale song, a warning you can hear from afar

Every kind of creature has its own call in its chatter: birds chirp and trill (the owl hoots), wolves and foxes bark and howl when angered, big beasts grunt and bellow, small ones squeak, bugs buzz and click, the snake hisses, toads croak, bats squeak, otters and beavers whistle

Every animal now fights its own way: rams back off and ram, stags charge in pairs, elk swing wide, bears swipe hard and short, badgers dig in, beavers block with their tails, lynxes pounce, foxes and martens go round to your back, snakes strike from hiding, moths flock to light, hedgehogs and woodlice roll up, snails leave slowing slime, glow-worms flash to slow you, and stoats, otters, squirrels and dormice dart and weave

Each new move shows clearly: glistening slime, a burst of glow-worm light, a ring of thrown-up earth round a dug-in badger, a beaver's raised tail and the glint of a blocked shot, spikes whirling round a rolling hedgehog
Try each new move in the arena: ?arena=ram, pair, wide, swipe, dig, block, flank, packflank, pounce, strike, moth, roll, woodlouse, slime, flash, weave, otter, squirrel, dart

fragments.title: A full-screen start screen
items: The start screen fills the window with big, easy-to-read text over the dimmed forest
"New in" this version lists each change with its own heading and bullets, dated, with the two versions before it underneath
"Coming up" lists the work in progress, straight from what the builders have open, so it's always current
On a phone, drag to scroll the text; a tap still starts
New sounds, all made in the music's key: a creature turning angry growls, one turning happy pops, and an invite ends in a flourish, fuller for bigger animals
Sleeping legends snore softly and dream in a quiet tone; a restless one's sleep turns uneasy; a legend winding up an attack sounds it a second before
Areas that have joined the party add their own beat to the music as you fly near
💌s get their sounds (a soft fire, a chime on a hit, a tick as the heart fills) as soon as they land
The miniature blur now covers the night sky too, so over the treetops the stars and moon soften with the edges of the picture instead of staying sharp
Your animals keep out of trouble on long trips: far from you on the ground (or from their sigil) they travel quietly along the edges between areas, a little faster, and wild animals leave them be
Close to you on the ground, or near their sigil, they're your posse again and fight as before; they don't drop out mid-fight
While an animal travels, its leash becomes its route: a dotted line on the ground from it to you or its sigil, snaking along the area borders (easy to see from the treetops)
Only your posse eats berries: travellers don't stop for them
The treehouse now stands due north of the dancefloor, just outside its ring of speakers, facing the floor
At the start the ley line runs from the treehouse's front straight south across the dancefloor, then curves off to the first soundsystem

Every kind of tree now grows from the same tree generator: spruces in tiered skirts, willows and weeping birches hung with curtains, banded birches, orange-barked pines, hollies with berries, yews, larches, alders and tree ferns, all a little bolder
Try ?style=bold or ?style=ref for a more pixel-art look on the trees
With ?style=bold or ?style=ref the little tufts on the ground get the pixel-art look too: fewer, bolder blades, moss and pebbles as lit domes, heather in flower, ferns with clear fronds
New controls: WASD to fly (arrows still work), the mouse to aim, left click throws 💌s
Right click dodges (Space too), Q rises or lands, E puts down a sigil or cycles them, R casts the speed spell
No more browser menu when you right click the game
Every area now starts with one young and one adult (was a baby and two adults), so the first areas you land in are easier to invite; they still grow by one creature a wave while wild
Legends sing like whales: long, deep, slow moans in a huge space; calm and rising when happy, groaning low when angry, wavering in a nightmare, and one long building swell before their big attack
A sleeping legend moans softly in its dreams now and then as you pass

New hats for the witches: none at all, a top hat, cowboy hat, straw conical hat, deely boppers, party hat, musketeer's plumed hat, a starry wizard's hat, a bobble beanie, a crown, a mushroom cap and a traffic cone
Scarves from short to trailing, bags of any size, and backpacks; hats, cloaks and brooms can go much further
Your witch cries out when she's hurt ("ouch!", "oof!", "eek!"), more strained on her last hit, and lets out a long "whoa-oh" when she's knocked down; the music dips for a moment

The party witches are all different now: each is a new witch from the witch generator, with bigger brims, longer cloaks and things both witchy and modern (a cat, crow, toad or bat riding along, a lantern, a potion, a spellbook, round shades, wristbands, bum bags, chunky trainers)
The pink heart meter over a creature you are inviting shows again as your 💌s land, and the fill tick sounds as it rises
When the party's over the music winds down like a record stopping, and each area has its own quiet night: wind in the pines, frogs in the bogs, owls and crickets in the woods, the sea at home
Sleeping animals snore softly near you
A small ring follows the mouse: pink within a 💌's reach, broken beyond it, and a blue arc fills round it while your dodge recharges
Dodging a moment too early still works: the dodge goes as soon as it's ready
An angry legend's note now says it also settles back to sleep when one of its children is back in its area

Each kind of place has its own mood in the dark: misty teal over the bogs and ponds, violet-grey in the dead and ancient woods, pale mist on the open moor, near-black under the pines; it shifts gently as you fly from one to the next
Behind the scenes: a new kind of area can now be added as a recipe of data alone, the first step towards many more areas

A soundsystem (or the home ring's speakers) under attack off screen shows a 🔇 at the screen's edge pointing to it, drawn in pixels like the 🎶 pointer: its ring is the soundsystem's health, draining as it's hit, the cue shakes at each blow, it says how far, and it flashes and fades if the soundsystem falls; one per soundsystem, up to three, on the ground and from the treetops (?debug=attack to see it)
The edge pointers' distances are one crisp pixel label each: pointers that would sit on one another are moved apart along the edge, and each label sits clear of its ring

A glint over a creature's head as it starts winding up a blow, dust kicked up behind a lunge, petals flying from a charging boar, a cold drift of motes round anything slowed, and a shockwave under a legend's blow
A legend no longer flashes the whole screen white when it's hit: its flash is half as strong, and the hit's star marks the blow

Attacks read better: creatures crouch as they wind up and stretch out as they lunge, a hit squashes its target and it springs back, a hard knock bowls it over once, and every blow lands with a crisp pixel star, a puff of dust and a spray of bits in that animal's own colours (or party confetti)
The debug overlay (~) shows what sound is actually leaving the game, and the playtest log (L) notes every time it goes silent while the music should be playing, with where you were
?micCheck=1 lets the game listen through the microphone for sound cutting out after it leaves the game (debug only)

The badger evolves: a fluffy cub that's all face, a low wedge-shaped young, a broad shaggy adult with pale digging claws, and the moor's legend, low as a boulder, with standing stones growing from its back, their runes lit by the moon
The beach is more irregular: wide sandy bays, narrow stretches, and rocky ones where the sand nearly vanishes
Shells, starfish, the odd conch and washed-up seaweed lie about the sand, and trails of footprints (bare feet, paws, hooves, birds) wander along it and fade away
The bushes at the edge of the woods follow the beach's bays and narrows, and stay clear of the shells and footprints
The woods now meet the beach in a scalloped edge of bushes, beach grass and the odd palm, with soft shade on the sand under them, instead of a grainy band
The hills near the coast no longer flatten out early, well before the beach starts
There are always witches on the beach now: a handful of them, each on her own, spread all the way round the island's coast
Lie down to stargaze on the beach and the world curves away so the whole night sky opens up over the sea
Stargaze together with a beach witch for a few seconds and little hearts float up off you both
Invitations that land on the beach or in the sea stay longer and fade slowly, bobbing on the water
A secret for explorers: fly to the very edge of the world and you'll find a beach, with the calm dark sea mirroring the moon and stars and the sound of waves
Keep flying out to sea and she lands on the sand and lies back to look at the stars
Now and then other witches are hanging out on the beach: land near them and you'll chat, hold hands, hug and stargaze together
A runestone's column of light now only appears when the ley line reaches it, shooting up with a flare
The rings of magic symbols round the runestones are gone: the ley line, its pulse and the beacons show what's coming
A "Player:" picker in the corner of her bedroom (for testing): pick a bot and cast the scroll to watch it play
Her bedroom is all one pixel art now: the menu, its tabs, sliders, buttons and writing are drawn in pixels at the room's own size, with a pixel title
The bedroom is laid out to fit your window: the tapestry menu down the left, the room centred beside it, and the spell scroll in the corner
Nothing on the ground shows through the curve of the world any more: invitations, hearts, chat bubbles and the angry and dazed marks past the horizon are hidden by the earth
The music waits for the first home speaker, then grows a layer with each one that comes alive, until the twelfth makes it whole
The music while the home speakers boot up no longer loops its tune: a new melody every 16 bars

The game now starts when you cast the party spell: a ley line runs round the dancefloor's ring of runestones, clockwise from the top, and its pulse turns each stone into a speaker; when the last one turns, the first wave's countdown begins
In the bot game the skilled witch now does a few legend quests, brings relics to the legends by the coming waves, and leads her young creatures to berries
Bot game: a button on the start screen to watch the skilled bot play a whole run (or ?bot=skilled, ?bot=crude); its tag says what she's doing, 1×/2×/4× speeds it up, Esc comes back

Fourteen new brooms to pick in the creator: a missile, a curled tip, handlebars, a hobby horse, a jet bike, an oar, a mop, a pitchfork, a canoe, a ladder, a speeder bike, a bicycle, a quad drone and a gyrocopter, each in your own two colours, with flames, spinning wheels, rotors and propellers, and drips

No more round window in the canopy round you on the ground: the trees thin out crown by crown, each tree and its trunk fading as one, with a ragged edge that drifts slowly and leans the way you're flying
Flying over the treetops, the witch's light warms the crowns under her instead of turning them bright green
Charging animals (boars, elk, stags, rams, hedgehogs, woodlice) now run much further, carrying their momentum past you in wide arcs before they come round again
A charging animal hurts anyone it touches on its way, not only at the end; a lynx's pounce carries on through you
Fights with chargers and lynxes are much more dangerous: keep moving and blink across their lane
A wild animal knocked down in a fight now lies stunned for 20 seconds before it runs off, plenty of time to win it over with 💌s
Wild animals now chase you up to 30 m outside their area, then give up and trot back home instead of waiting at the edge
When its area's party comes, the baby in a legend's circle dances there in its circle instead of going off to the soundsystem
A sleeping legend's circle now lies well away from its area's runestone, never beside the soundsystem's party
A sleeping legend's circle is a safe place: nothing outside it can attack you while you're inside, and anything chasing you gives up
The map is round now: about 196 areas in a circle round home, then a ring of quiet forest with nothing to do in it before the edge
Flying out to the edge slows you gently and drifts you back in, instead of a hard wall (?shape=square brings back the old square map)
The game clock starts when she casts the party spell; until then a prompt under it says which key casts it
Controls: Space rises and lands, E puts a sigil down, Q cycles your sigils (on the ground too), and the mouse wheel zooms
In the creator she can't keep still: she fixes her hat, twirls, bounces, laughs, looks out of the window, practises a step and looks round the room, and spins to show off each change you make
The fairy lights round her room come on one by one as the forest grows, and flash when it's ready
The character creator wears the game's lantern amber (its Start button, sliders and chosen options), to match the in-game HUD
On a slow machine, the forest no longer stalls loading while the creator is open
Dressing her up: each thing she wears has its own box with its own colour picker, one open at a time
Walk her up to her things in the bedroom (the rail, the mirror, the hats, the broom...) to open their box
Character creator: seven looks to start from (Classic, Raver, Forest witch, Night owl, Disco, Rodeo, DJ)
🎲 Randomise now picks colours that go together
Sliders snap to her own look as you pass it, and a double-click puts one back
The creator's sections fold away: a first visit opens just the looks, the hat and the colours
The broom has a thickness slider beside its length, for every kind of broom (a skinny stick to a fat missile or a tub of a canoe), saved with her and drawn in flight and on the party witches

Every slider in the character creator now changes her for every option: the hat's lean works on every hat, the little hat's height, brim and band work, the traffic cone's base and stripes and the crown's and mushroom's glow follow the brim and band sliders; and sliders that can't apply are greyed out (no hat's height, a beanie's brim, a canoe's bend, a drone's bristles, no cloak's length)

With ?style=bold or ?style=ref the oaks, beeches, limes and other broadleaf trees get the pixel-art look too: each crown lit as one shape, bright on its top-left and shaded below, with clustered tones

Her room shows sooner when the game opens, and the forest is ready sooner behind it
Wolves stand taller and leaner on long legs, the adults with a shaggy mane
Badgers are low, wide and flat, on short thick legs
Boars carry a big shoulder hump and a heavy front end
Bears are massive, with a high shoulder hump and pillar legs
The boot's ley line now runs through the dancefloor's stones, and each turns into its speaker as the sparkler touches it
The boot's pulse burns like the sparkler, and at the end of the boot it carries straight on as the wave's pulse: one sparkler, no gap
Behind the sparkler the ley line is a thin line of ash, and the line's growing end just finishes plainly
Every few seconds a faint ripple runs along each ley line, showing which way it goes
Hedgehogs bristle with long spines past their outline
Toads sit squat and wide, their eyes standing up like domes

The knockdown candles now stand along the front edge of the treehouse's terrace, a long loading bar you can read at the normal zoom
Trees behind a fading crown no longer vanish: no more patches of forest drawn as flat green haze with no trunks, or canopy cut off along straight lines
Firs, cedars, willows and yews show their trunks under their low crowns, so a Norway forest on the ground has trunks again

Clear an area and its runestone turns into a soundsystem at once: invite every one of its wild animals, or see them run off (its sleeping legend and the baby in its circle don't count). Its babies dance, a party witch flies in and its music plays.

Every area is full of animals from the start, and the areas later on the route hold more. Heavy kinds come as a few big adults, swarms as many young. Each area has two babies. Nothing grows while you play any more.

The wild forest is darker while you explore
Your light grows slowly when a fight starts near you, and settles back afterwards

Creatures have character: each kind holds itself its own way (a proud stag, a low badger) and, standing about, does its own thing now and then: a wolf howls, a boar paws the ground, a squirrel flicks its tail, an otter shakes itself dry, a snake rises to look about
Happy creatures and your party animals give a little bounce of joy now and then
The game runs smoother with every area full of animals: each step of the rules takes about half the time it did.
Dark-coated legends (the bear, the boar, the raven and others as dark) no longer vanish into the night
Behind her decks you can hear her: a quiet scratch when she rocks the record, and a little "woo-hoo!" when she throws a hand up
After the party spell, her room's record keeps crackling softly until the first speaker brings the music in
Dolphins leap out of the sea off the east coast at night, alone or in pairs
Off the west coast, very rarely, something huge stirs in the moonlit water
An easy quest early on: one of the first three areas the party reaches has a sleeping legend that dreams of a baby from another of those first three
Five eerie old trees now stand somewhere in every forest: a bleached dead tree, a hunched gnarled one, a fat hollow trunk, a dead tree cleft in two, and one bowed right over into an arch
The game opens faster: her room shows sooner while the witch, her treehouse and the soundsystems are drawn in the background
The game gets going faster: the dancefloor's light patterns for every area are made about three times as fast as it loads.
Fewer hitches in play: the game's shaders are all made ready while the forest grows, not the first time you rise, land or come near something new
Legend carvings are made in quiet moments, not the moment you first fly near one
Fireworks over a cleared area now whoosh, boom and crackle, and the party under them cheers

Bringing a legend what it dreams of now makes its whole area friendly at once: the creatures already living there stop attacking her (any mid-fight calm down and drop their sieges), not only the ones grown there afterwards

On computers whose graphics card can't hold a very large texture, the forest floor now shows each area's own ground (moss, paths, ponds) instead of one plain earth everywhere, and the game uses far less memory
Beards of pale moss and dark vines hang from the trees in the wet, old and tangled woods (the wispy forest, the bog, the ancient wood and others), draped from the crowns, trunks and low branches
Knocked down with your hat on, it slowly floats off and down beside you while the rest of the screen dims
Knocked down, the screen closes in on your fallen hat, which spins into a record, rewinds with a scratch and opens on you back at your decks
Herons step their long legs when they walk
Owls, ravens, hedgehogs and moles step their feet in turn
An area's animals fight you while you're in their area, and lose interest and go home once you leave it, as before
Every time you're knocked down the beat speeds up by 1 BPM for the rest of the run: the music quickens and the waves come a little sooner. The tempo shows on the wave pointer and over your decks

Knocked out, your hat floats to the ground, then you scratch behind your decks until you can fly again: about six seconds in all, a little longer each time you are knocked down again soon after, a countdown over you, while your animals fight on without you

Knocked down and back at her decks, a loading bar of candles along the desk's front shows her wait: a white candle for every second of it, red ones for the extra from being knocked down again soon after, burning down from the red end while she scratches, the last guttering out as she's back
Sleeping legends now dream of creatures from deeper in the forest, further along the party's path

The ley line never kinks: it sweeps through each runestone in one smooth curve and never turns tighter than 25 m (leyLines.minRadius); where the next stone lies back the way it came, it loops round the stone instead of doubling back in a hairpin

A legend's dream bubble and its circle's notes keep clear of the legend itself

Losing a soundsystem speeds the pulse up to meet the sooner wave, instead of making it jump

The dancefloor ring's runestones are turned like its speakers: the far ones face the dancefloor and the near ones face out to us

The dancefloor ring's runestones are carved with three glowing dots, one above another: the speaker each will become

Every soundsystem now projects its area's animal sigil into the sky as a flickering hologram over the treetops, in place of its lasers; it glitches when the soundsystem is hurt and folds away when it falls
Her claw slashes are twice as big and glow bright red like the berries, easy to read from the ground and the treetops

Every area's soundsystem is its own now: grown from a generator, no two alike, turned towards the dancefloor and bigger the further out it stands

Soundsystems stand on the ground again instead of sinking into it
The string lights are back in six bright colours
Each area's wild swarm now grows along the runestone order, from a single young at the first stone to about 12 at the last, mostly young near home and mostly adults far out

Every kind of animal is equally dangerous: strong kinds (bears, boars, stags…) come as at most 6 tough ones, light kinds (hedgehogs, bats, beetles…) as up to 16 small ones, and the forest holds fewer wild animals than before

How often the waves come is now a dropdown in the top right of your bedroom, and every game starts at the usual pace unless you pick another (it's no longer remembered from last time)
Creatures are half again as big, so they're easier to make out; legends grew too, to stay well above their adults
Hurt animals leave little dark-red footprints (and the badly hurt, drips) that fade after a few seconds; healing stops them

A singing voice now carries half of every melody
The tempo stays at 120 all run, 5 faster each time you're knocked down
Knocked down, the record scratches and the music stops; back at your decks you drop the needle on a new record, scratch a little routine (different every time) and the new tunes start from the top

Green + signs float up off an animal whenever it is healed: a berry, invited, leashed, or a happy legend mending (one small + every second or two)

On the ground, hold the sigil button with nothing to pick up to put your hat down; press it over the hat to put it back on
The giant party bottles now lie in the forest where a relic waits, half-buried and glowing in their own colour

When a soundsystem falls, its party witch stays and lies down out past the speakers to stargaze, in pairs and threes
When the party is over, all the party witches lie looking up at the sky; keep still beside one and she will get up to chat, hold hands, hug and stargaze with you
Swooping ravens, owls and bats linger 4 s at the bottom of each dive (was 2, 2 and 1), so you have time to invite them

The temple ruins come in many more shapes, different on every island: a round temple, a long colonnade, a temple on its podium, a fallen pediment, a portico half buried in a mound, an overgrown theatre
Small classical ruins scatter more widely: a few columns, a lone column, a doorway, an altar on its steps
Winning an island gets its own victory music: the night's drop a step higher, a choir and strings over it, and claps for the conga line
Each campaign has its own world: its islands keep their shapes night after night, while the forest, scenery, animals and legends on them change each night
The sea chart shows your world's seed to share; Start over begins a new world, random or from a seed you type in (or add ?world= to the link)
Through the boot, the dancefloor writes the island's sigil, the World Tree, stroke by stroke as the pulse goes round the ring
The sea chart has much more open sea: islands sit further apart, never closer than a wide strait, with the phases mixed together
Islands turn to fit their neighbours, arms into bays, and the outer islands reach their arms out to sea
The sea chart's islands are packed over the whole sea instead of sitting on rings: clusters and open water, each island still roughly in its direction and further out by phase
Neighbouring islands' coasts follow each other across a strait, and no island overlaps another
Sailing to an island: the fly-in now plays in full after the island loads, instead of cutting straight to your decks
While the island loads, the chart's last picture stays up with a "landing…" note
Sailing to an island from the sea chart now flies you in: over the sea from the south, low over the forest, up over the dancefloor and the Ent, and down to your decks (any key skips)
A campfire crackles beside every witch on the beach, to one side of her so she's never hidden
Half as many shells, pebbles, seaweed and footprint trails on the beach

On the sea chart, the special lakes (ice, lava, oases, sinkholes, tarns, hot springs, rainbow pools and lily ponds) start a phase earlier: about half the lakes in the third ring of islands are special, and all of them further out
The bot game's witch leaves a few fighters on guard at home when she passes by with plenty following her
Five new brooms to pick in your room's Broom box
Battering: your blinks stun the creatures in your path
Ley jump: press R to jump to the ley line's pulse
Haul: your sigils pull on you half as hard
Ground pound: press R to rise or land at once, knocking creatures back; landing stuns them
Stealth: creatures don't see you unless you're inviting, or putting something down or picking it up
Speech and thought bubbles point at their speaker's head now, not the middle of its body, and follow it as it turns and moves

On the sea chart, each island's land and lakes follow its place on the compass, blending between neighbours: ice in the far north, lava in the volcanic east, oases in the southern desert, deep cliff-walled sinkholes in the western jungle, and glacial tarns, terraced, steaming hot springs, rainbow hot pools and lily ponds between; an island on a border has lakes of both kinds
The sea chart shows the islands at their true sizes, packed over the whole sea, each coast following its neighbour's across a narrow strait
The sea chart paints each island like a real map: green lowlands, uplands, rock and peaks, darker forests, in its biome's colours (cold, hot, rocky, jungle and the rest)
Lakes on the sea chart's islands, pale water lying in the hills
The sea chart's island sigils grow more detailed as you zoom in: carved bands, then a solid carved emblem
Zoom right in on an island on the sea chart: it fills the screen, its hills shaded, each area's ground in its own colour, the sea pale in the shallows round its coast
On the map table the moon rises over the north-west edge as it opens, then circles slowly, and every island casts its shadow across the sea
The map table has open sea round its edge
The map table and the sea chart open at once after the first time: every island is made once and kept
For testing: a "🧪 Test: sail anywhere" button on the sea chart (and at the map table) lets you sail to any island with a creature, found or not, without changing your save
The hot springs on the map table steam again
Sailing from the sea chart flies you in: the camera glides to the island, its sigil settling onto its glowing dancefloor, then swoops down to its south coast before the night begins (any key skips)
Shadows are coloured, not black: a campfire's throws a cool blue-violet, and runestones and soundsystems cast a soft shade of their own glow
A sleeping legend's dream bubble is as big as its speech bubble now, and the sleepers' 😴s grow with them too
An area whose legend's quest you've done no longer turns on you when its wave comes: its animals stay friendly, so the night can always be won
A happy creature carries its sigil a little to the south of it, the same distance a parked creature rests from its placed sigil; pick it up there
A happy creature's rune shows through grass, bushes and trees, as a placed sigil does
Pick your hat's and broom's powers from a dropdown in your room's Hat and Broom boxes
The Harvest hat's berries now grow on little seedlings
The Cyclone hat raises a swirling whirlwind you can see
The chosen hat power shows its little icon
Five new hats to pick in your room's Hat box
Harvest: put it down and six berries grow round it
Dowsing: put it down and a pointer leads you to the nearest relic for a minute
Sentry: put it down and it throws 💌s at wild creatures nearby
Slingshot: 💌s you throw past it circle it, then fly off at a creature further away
Gathering: put it down, then pick it up again, and every sigil you placed within 100 m comes back to you
Five more hats to pick in your room's Hat box
Bramble: wild creatures within 30 m of it are slowed
Mine: put it down and it stuns wild creatures within 15 m
Lullaby: put it down and wild creatures nearby fall asleep; a 💌 wakes one up
Cyclone: a whirlwind sweeps creatures round it, lifts them up and flings them away
Nursing: your own creatures near it heal
The soundsystems' sky sigils no longer show through the ground past the horizon

Home is now all green woods and mostly furry friends: a fox in the old oaks, a hare in the bluebell glade, a mole in the fern forest, a badger in the wispy forest, a stoat in the alder forest, a squirrel in the twiggy forest and a pine marten in the old pinewood
The owl, toad and beetle now live further out, on the islands
The owl now nests at the stone shrine, glowworms light the meadow, the boar roots in the grassland, woodlice live on the moor, the snake basks on Norway's slate and the wolf prowls the lost garden
Islands from phase 1 have lakes: a few areas of water, never by home, with small shores where the forest floor runs down into the water (no beaches)
Lake water is a lighter blue than the sea, with the stars and the moon in it, and some lakes have big koi, about the size of a baby animal
You can fly over a lake in the treetops but can't land on it; on foot you stop at the shore, and so do the animals, who walk round
Sailing to an island lands sooner: its forest is drawn while you look at it on the chart and fly in
Your animals following you across the island walk round lakes along the shore, and their dotted trail shows the way they really go, instead of cutting straight over the water
On a new island, the treehouse Ent rides on the back of a giant party legend of that island's kind (try ?carrier=bear to see one at home)
A new animal for the badlands: the meerkat, scurrying about its red-rock warren under twisted junipers and sitting up as a lookout when it stops
Its legend's boon, Lookout: your 💌s reach further

Esc's pause now slides every test slider in down the left, see-through and grouped by the change that added it (newest first), with nothing else over the game: changes show at once, and Copy values copies them all to paste back
New sliders there for the bubbles' sizes (a baby's, an adult's, a legend's)
Each island's outer woods now grow the same kinds of trees as the areas next to them, so every island has its own forest right to the shore
Landing on an island is quicker: fewer kinds of tree to draw
A happy creature near you brings its sigil to your feet from any side, walking round you and your animals
Runestones', soundsystems' and ruins' shadows fade in softly at their base instead of starting hard
Every area's runestone is a little different now: 20 weathered shapes, some mirrored, with the carving always the right way round
Scenery's shadows taper at the base like the trees' do, wider pieces opening out over more ground
Temples, castles, ruins, set pieces, relics, runestones and soundsystems now cast shadows from your glow and the campfires, like the tree trunks
Sigils on the ground sit on a dark patch and show in full colour, so you can read them on bright ground and on the dancefloor
No more black circle round a sigil you put down after visiting the treehouse or a legend's circle
Sigils on the ground are easier to read: no more glow washing them into a bright blob on lit grass
The same calmer sigils in your stack, from the treetops, and on a creature walking home
The sound cuts out less: the singer's effects use half the work they did, the costliest go first if the sound struggles, and only so many sound effects play at once (the nearest and most important)
Pause page: a slider for how many sound effects play at once
The light round a partying soundsystem no longer blows out to white: the ground stays lit and coloured with its grass showing
Pause page (Esc): sliders for the light's knee and ceiling, the soundsystem's light and the bloom threshold
Every hat and broom in the creator now has its own little pixel icon
The treehouse is now a round deck up on the Ent: land on it from the treetops, walk round it, and time runs ten times slower while you're up there
Your DJ decks sit along the deck's front edge, where each night starts
The world map stands in the deck's middle: press E at it to open the sea chart and sail off from there whenever you like (mid-night, that ends the night unwon)
The treehouse Ent is here: a great kneeling tree holding the deck up, its lanterns lit, your decks along its front
The map table shows a living miniature of the sea chart, and E there opens the chart itself over the game
Land on the treehouse deck and press F (or the Bedroom button) to go back to your room mid-night: change your look, hat and broom while the world runs ten times slower
'Back to the island' (where the party scroll was) takes you back to the deck
Leave a hat lying somewhere and fetch a new one from your room: the old one stays where it is, still working its spell, and you can have several out at once
You can only pick up a hat from the ground when you aren't wearing one: put yours down first
Every hat you've left out gets its own pointer, its hat in that hat's colour, and keeps the look it had when you put it down
The pause page has every trunk-shadow control: style (soft, hard, off), core, width and a campfire's reach, beside darkness, length and your glow's reach and height
Tree shadows fade in from the foot of the trunk and pinch in there, so wide roots don't splay out strangely
Tree shadows fade away as you walk right up to the tree, from your glow and from campfires
Tree shadows now darken the grass and flowers they fall on, not just the ground
Longer, darker tree shadows that reach further from your glow, and campfires that light further
On foot at night, tree trunks and beach palms cast shadows from your own glow and from campfires, swinging round you as you walk

Clearing every area on the island wins the night straight away: two fast finale pulses race from where the wave's pulse is, one home and one on to the end of the ley line, fireworks at every stone they pass
The beach witches and the party witches chat in the same pixel speech bubbles as you and the animals

Bear cubs, otter pups, beaver kits, baby dormice, toadlets and mole pups now look like babies (round, big-eyed, short-legged; the mole pup pink, the toadlet all head and eyes), and the young are lanky or slim, growing into the adults rather than being small copies of them
A new kind of area for the cold north's island, the snowfield: deep snow under snow-laden firs and dwarf birch, and a ring of old stones half buried in a drift

The arctic fox, a new creature for it: a small white fox with a huge brush that leaps on you like a fox mousing in the snow; its legend is the oldest of the white foxes, shaggy and frost-muzzled, with one vast tufted brush and stone beads round its legs, and its gift is Arctic fox's Snow pounce (a longer blink, and quicker starts on foot)
The glowing dotted edges round the party's areas are gone (a pause-page switch brings them back)
A new animal for the badlands: the armadillo, trundling through its scrub wash among thorn trees and junipers, and charging you curled up
Its legend rolls about as a glowing ball, the seams between its bands alight
Its legend's boon, Roll: a little longer blink, and untouchable a little longer after it
The otter legend now stands like the others (creatures never go in the water), its stone and glowing pearl worn on a cord at its throat

Every area now has its own main tree: the crags' larches bent by the wind, mossy firs in the mistwood, stunted rowans on the icefall, ancient weeping birches in the trollwood and wind-bent junipers on the snowfield
The music should stop cutting out on busy laptops: the sound now asks for a bigger output buffer, and a computer that still struggles asks for more next time
The music stays on the beat the game shows, scheduled early by the sound's own delay
The badlands grow a few more kinds of tree: hawthorns and pines among the junipers, which now have leafy skirts below their crowns
The beach's sand is pixelated like everything else now, chunky and grainy instead of smooth
The bedroom shows which version you're playing, small in its top left corner
Herons grow their plumes as they age, and the heron legend is now a tall elder carrying a softly glowing paper lantern in its bill
Baby ravens are downy fledglings with stubby tails
Baby snakes have bigger heads, and their markings come in as they grow
Each area's trees and bushes reach twice as far into its neighbours, so the planting blends across the borders
Where two areas meet, their trees and bushes now mix one by one across the border instead of in clumps
Coming down from the treetops, the canopy now opens round you smoothly as the camera comes down, and closes as you rise, instead of switching all at once
In the treetops the forest canopy now reaches the horizon even when the game is drawing less scenery to keep up its frame rate (no more circle of trees round you)

A new creature for the hot south: the cheetah, slim and long-legged with black spots, tear lines and a long ringed tail, and its own area, the Plains: open short grass, small thorn trees and tall termite mounds
The cheetah's legend, asleep in the grass, gives Cheetah's Sprint: quicker on foot
Trees and bushes turning see-through in front of the witch no longer look milkier than the rest, so no ring shows round her in the forest
Switches to find the circle round the witch: ?occ=off, ?hole=off, ?hole=all and ?seedepth=off in the link; L's playtest log notes where she was and how it was seen when pressed
Every shadow takes its colour from the light it lies in: blue-violet by a campfire, a warm shade in the moonlight (under the creatures and the witch, and the trees' and scenery's)
Anything standing in a tree's or a ruin's shadow is darkened by it too, not just the ground: creatures, the witch, bushes and props
One "Shadow colour" slider on the pause page for them all

Animals are no longer sausages: a body can have a deep, wide chest and a slim waist (its width and depth set apart along its length). The big cats, the wolf, fox and fennec, and the stag, roe and elk have theirs
Eight animals grow up instead of just growing: the lynx, cheetah, cat, boar, raccoon, red panda, polar bear and meerkat are slight and long-legged when young and deep in the chest as adults

Four-legged creatures' faces have bones now: a brow over the eyes, cheeks, a lower jaw with a mouth, and whiskers on the ones that have them, so a lynx reads as a cat and a bear as a bear from the front

Four-legged creatures have real legs now: an elbow and a wrist in front, a stifle and a hock behind, each kind standing its own way (deer and boar up on slim cannons and hooves, cats and dogs on their toes, bears and badgers flat-footed, newts sprawling), with paws and hooves in place of balls

Animals can have a spine of their own along the back, from a crest to a groove: the big cats and the wolf carry a groove between their back muscles, the stag and elk a shoulder line, the boar a bristled crest

Four-legged creatures have a frame under their coats now: withers over the shoulders, a pelvis at the rump, a dip between, a deep chest in front of the forelegs, and a neck with a nape and a throat, so the head hangs from the neck instead of being skewered on it

A new creature, the crocodile, with its own area, the mangrove swamp: long, low and toothy, it lies in wait and lunges when you come close. Its legend sleeps in the mud like a log, a ridge of standing stones down its back, and its gift is Crocodile's Snap (your blink comes back quicker). It lives on a later island, out to the south-west
The fight and world test knobs (fight scale, speed and momentum, treetop speed, area size) moved from the debug overlay's bottom-left panel onto the pause page's sliders (Esc)
Two new animals for the mangrove swamp islands: the dragonfly, darting and hovering over dark pools among the mangroves, and the fiddler crab, scuttling sideways across the mudflats
Their legends: a dragonfly that is all eye and wing, and a crab with one colossal gleaming claw it waves to beckon you
The drowned wood's larches look drowned: swollen at the waterline, their crowns dark and dying, hung with weed and moss
The fox's legend is now an old shrine fox: nine silver-tipped tails, a grizzled muzzle and a bitten ear, a red rope and bell at its throat, rings in its ears
The ram's legend is now the old bellwether: weathered horns ringed in bronze with one tip broken, a bell at its throat and a garland of heather

Legends can show their age and their standing now: a grey muzzle and brows, an ear bitten in some old fight, a tusk or horn broken short, a bronze torc, rings on horns and tusks, earrings, cuffs on their legs, little bells. The ram's horns are ringed, a bell at each tip; the shrine fox has rings in its ears and a bell at its throat

The legends are elders of their kind now: the moon-hare with its immense veined ears and the moon behind it, the snail whose shell holds the night sky, the hedgehog hung with offerings, the raccoon thief-king in its stolen crown and trinkets

More elders: the squirrel with its vast curled tail and acorn beads, the dormouse hugging its own tail under a crown of hazelnuts, the blind mole king with gold claws and a lantern, the badger with chalk lines down its back and a bronze torc
And the marten with its shield-shaped blaze and amber pendant, the meerkat sentinel on its tower of red stones, and the armadillo's ball worn like ancient armour

Five legends are now elders of their kind: the stoat an old dark-brown ermine with a garland, the bear grizzled and mossy with a bell at its throat, the polar bear scarred under a crown of ice, the Komodo dragon crowned with spines, and the red panda grizzled under a wreath
The adult bear has a bigger hump
A new creature for the jungle west: the elephant, the biggest animal in the forest, with a trunk, great fan ears and tusks
Its legend is the elder of the elephants, an ancient matriarch, her trunk raised, her tusks banded in bronze, hung with temple bells, a jewelled brow-cloth and a garland of flowers
Its own area, the Temple jungle: strangler figs and kapoks over red earth, and a heap of tumbled temple stones in the clearing
The elephant's legend gives Elephant's Trumpet: bigger 💌s that carry further
The Erg grows thorn trees and the odd baobab among its date palms, and its saltbush now shows
A new creature for the hot south: the fennec fox, a small sand fox that's mostly ears, and its own area, the Erg: dunes, date palms round an oasis and a ring of sandstone round an old hearth
The fennec's legend, asleep under the sand, gives Fennec's Ears: 💌s reach further
A new animal for a later island: the flying squirrel of the Mistwood, a misty old-growth forest of giant spruce, cedar and tree ferns with a nurse log in its clearing
Flying squirrels glide from spot to spot through the trees, and swoop in on a glide when they fight
Its legend's gliding skin is a starry night sky; at peace it gives Glide: a little quicker over the treetops and a longer blink
A new kind of area for the frozen north's island, the trollwood: weeping birch hung with frost and dark pines in stands, an iced stream, and snow-capped boulders that might be sleeping trolls

The frost troll, a new creature for it: a hunched, shaggy troll with big round eyes, a rosy bulb of a nose and a white beard, knuckling along on its long arms, slow but hard-hitting; its legend is the oldest troll, half turned to stone from its feet up, beads round its neck, and its gift is Frost troll's Long stride (quicker on foot, and a quicker climb to the treetops)

A new creature for the mountains and glaciers: the frost wyrm, a wingless ice dragon with great swept-back horns, and its own area, the Frost cave: glacier ice, frozen falls, stunted firs and crystal-leaf trees
Its legend is the elder of all wyrms: aeons old, scarred, one horn broken, an icicle beard, its hoard frozen into its belly. It gives Wyrm's Glide: a longer blink
A new creature for the mountains and glaciers: the griffin, an eagle's head and wings on a lion's body, and its own area, the Eyrie: high scree peaks, lone cedars bent flat by the wind, a great nest
Its legend is the elder of all griffins, a battle-scarred guardian in an old gold harness. It gives Griffin's Talon: 💌s fly a quarter faster
On foot in the forest the picture draws faster: the trees were being drawn twice over (once more for the see-through parts over the witch), and crowns hidden in the gap round her were still drawn

Eight more animals grow up instead of just getting bigger: a round, big-eared arctic fox kit, a squirrel and a stoat young with short tails and big heads, a newt whose crest comes in, a salamander whose tail thickens (its legend crowned with fire), a flying squirrel whose membrane spreads (glowing on its legend), a pine marten whose tail gets fluffier, and a Komodo dragon with a long heavy head and a dewlap

A new creature, the hydra, with its own area, the drowned wood: a many-headed serpent of the black water, one head as a baby and up to seven when grown, each crested with spines. Its legend sleeps half under the water like a heap of drowned roots, its necks ringed in old bronze and two cut-off necks grown back as two heads each; its gift is Hydra's Many Heads (your 💌s come quicker and land a little more easily). It lives on a far island, out to the south-south-west

A new kind of area for the north-east's mountain island, the crags: lichened rock and glacier ice, rock spires, wind-bent larch and gnarled wild olives, broom, juniper and heather among the stones, and a heap of glacier rubble

The ibex, a new creature for it: a stocky wild goat whose horns grow from nothing on the kid to great knobbled scimitars, that backs off and charges like the ram; its legend is the peaks' oldest ibex, its horns grown vast and knobbled, a long beard, lichen on its flanks and stone beads round its legs, and its gift is Ibex's Sure-footed (quicker starts on foot, and a quicker climb to the treetops)
A new creature for the jungle west: the black jaguar, stocky and big-headed, black with rosettes a shade darker that show only in the light

Its legend is the elder of the jaguars: a huge head and crushing jaw, a grey muzzle, old scars, its hidden rosettes surfacing in the moonlight and rippling as it moves, a collar of jade and bronze beads
Its own area, the River jungle: a dark river under rainforest giants hung with lianas, vinewood glowing in the gloom, and a heap of mossed, fallen giants by the water
The jaguar's legend gives Jaguar's Night eyes: 💌s fly further and a little faster
Lions, bears and stags keep their coat colour on their lower jaw, and open mouths show just their fangs (a stag two small front teeth) instead of a pale block of teeth
The stag legend's flaming antlers sweep back instead of towering three times its height
A new animal for the rocky island to the east: the Komodo dragon, a huge lizard with a flicking forked tongue, in its own dry, rocky savannah of acacias and fan palms

Ten legends are now the ancient elders of their kinds: the wolf howls rings of moonlight, the stag's huge antlers burn at every tip, the elk carries glowing pools in its antlers, the bear towers with glowing claws, the otter floats on its back holding a pearl, the beaver grips a gnawed log, the toad swells a glowing throat sac, the owl stares from an enormous ringed face, the lynx has long glowing ear plumes and the boar ploughs up the earth

Ten legends redrawn as the ancient elders of their kind: the raven's hoard of tarnished coins, rings and keys; the bat's towering ears and sonar; the moth's staring eyes; the snake's shed skin; the salamander's glowing coals; the newt's tall sail; the heron on one stilt leg in its pool; the spider's rose-window web; the stag beetle's antler jaws; the woodlouse grown into a little house
Fewer hitches in the treetops: the game makes much less garbage each frame (the wave pointer, the party pieces, the creatures and the lights), so the browser pauses to collect it less often

A new creature for the hot south: the lion, a big tawny cat with a dark mane and a tufted tail, and its own area, the Savanna: tall gold grass under flat-topped acacias and baobabs, a kopje of sun-warmed boulders
The lion's legend, asleep in the long grass, gives Lion's Pride: 💌s fly a little faster and further

The map table on the treehouse deck shows the islands' real coastlines, and on the sea chart each island rises out of the sea as it's charted (no round stand-ins); the chart opens without the pauses the islands' arrival used to cause
The meadow's animal is now the wildcat, a stocky striped tabby that pounces, in place of the glow-worm; its legend is the meadow's old queen, white-whiskered and crowned in gold
The meadow has a few more trees and small copses
The wildcat's legend gives Paw prints: your 💌s leave a trail that lands too
Frost trolls, hedgehogs, armadillos and crabs change as they grow: a troll's first tusks and moss, a hoglet's soft spines, an armadillo pup's soft pink shell, a crab's claws growing with age

Animals open their jaws: wolves, lions, bears, crocodiles and the rest bite with their mouths open at the end of a wind-up and through a lunge, a legend roars as it wakes or turns, and a napping animal yawns as it gets up
A new animal for the cold island to the north: the penguin, waddling about and belly-sliding at you in a fight, in its own snowy rookery on a rocky shore
Its legend is an ancient penguin god, weathered like sea rock, its chick at its feet; happy, it gives Penguin's Toboggan: quicker on foot

A new creature, the polar bear, with its own area, the pack ice: white floes split by black water, a pressure ridge in the middle, wind-bent firs on the shore. It pounces from out of reach. Its legend has a vast shaggy coat streaming back off it, frost on its muzzle, and sleeps sunk in the ice like a drift of old snow; its gift is Polar bear's Blizzard (💌s fly further and land more easily). It lives on a later island, out to the north
Soundsystems and runestones light up the trees round them: trees and scenery near one now cast shadows away from its glow, as they do round a campfire
Clearings round soundsystems and runestones are smaller: the trees come in to about 15 m
A new animal for the cold rainforest: the raccoon, in its bandit mask, prowling a mossy creek under towering spruces and cedars
Its legend's boon, Light fingers: quicker 💌 bursts

Two new animals for the badlands islands: the rattlesnake, sidewinding across the cactus flats and rattling its warning when you come near, and the scorpion, out on the red canyon's rocks under the moon
Their legends: an ancient horned rattlesnake on great coils whose rattle ripples the sand, and an elder scorpion carrying its young on its back, glowing blue-green at its seams
A new animal for a later island: the red panda of the misty terraces, rusty red with a ringed tail, and its elder legend, an old white-whiskered mountain sage

Six animals reshaped after Ed's review: the polar bear carries its head low on a longer neck over a high shoulder, the unicorn stands tall on long legs with a horse's head, the badger has shoulders and a waist and a wedge of a head, the rhino's horn grows with it and its young is its own, the crocodile's wide flat jaws show their line and its legs splay out, and the snow leopard has longer legs, a thicker tail and big paws

A new creature, the rhino, with its own area, the bushveld (close thorn scrub on red earth): a grey hulk with a great horn on its nose that lowers its head and charges. Its legend is an elder with one colossal horn ringed in bronze offerings, a hide in heavy armour folds and old scars, and sleeps sunk in the red earth like a boulder; its gift is Rhino's Charge (much faster on the ground, slower to get going). It lives on a later island, out to the south

On the ground, four-legged creatures' legs bend where their species' do: a deer's hock high and sharp over an upright cannon, a bear's flat foot, a wolf's wrist, following the creature art instead of one guessed bend for all
A new animal: the roe deer, small and quick, all ears and eyes, living in a new kind of place, the mossy dell (rowan, birch and oak over deep moss and ferns), on an island far to the north-west
Its legend's gift, Spring: your dodge comes back sooner
The roe deer's legend is now the elder of the roe: an ancient grey-muzzled buck with heavy, mossy, many-tined antlers, a pale winter ruff and bead offerings round its legs
The mossy dell grows mostly rowan now, with birch and oak
The savanna's acacias stand in groves, the baobabs have shoots and low boughs round their trunks, and the plains' termite mounds stand taller
The Sentry hat throws its 💌s as far as the witch does (33 m)

A happy animal's sigil lies just below its feet, whatever its size: a mouse's close, an elephant's further off, so you always see the whole sigil (and a parked animal rests the same way above its own)
Sigils on the ground can be picked up from a quarter further away
A new kind of area for the high glaciers' island, the icefall: glacier ice and old snow, cairns and leaning standing stones, stunted pines, rowan and dwarf birch in the lee of the rocks
