Harder fights: creatures run 20% faster, their ranged attacks reach 20% further and adults are stronger, each with a Difficulty slider on the pause page.
Packs grow sooner and with each island's size: most areas start with more creatures, and only the largest islands' last areas field the biggest packs.
The spark's speed now rises in a straight line with the tempo: 1 m/s at 100 bpm, 1.8 at the usual 120, 3 at 150 and 5 at 200, with two Difficulty sliders for the 100 and 200 bpm speeds.
The berry you'd feed now glows brighter, with just the button (E, or your controller's) over it and a little arrow pointing at it: no words
An animal you've told to eat a berry goes and eats it before it joins any fight, then fights as usual

Brew Silent Film for a scratched sepia film with a narrow soundtrack, or Contour Dream to see coloured height lines across the island and its animals. Folded Space lets you walk across giant creases in the landscape.
Your hat on the treehouse floor on your first morning shows again, lying on the floor where you can see it, even with you standing behind it
Adults on your leash now give you a buff by how their kind retreats: extra dashes, faster movement, further-flying invites, shots both ways, faster firing or chaining invites
Different kinds stack; two of the same kind count once. A legend on your leash counts as three
An adult's buff runs on berries: up to five pips, two minutes each, shown beside its sigil. Lead it past berries to keep it going
Each buff shows an icon beside its animal's sigil, and the chain to a buffing animal glows

Masterplan reveals animal destinations, pack formations and attack aims. Brew Mirrorball for a mirror moon that scatters light across the forest, Woodcut for an ink print, or Kaleidoscope for six mirrored views around the witch.
A new link, https://edsaperia.github.io/witch/?fresh=1, starts a brand-new game on the latest version every time, without touching your own saves.
Holding the bed button works reliably when visiting a friend.
Ten new mushroom recipes make trees walk or tower, turn bark and light loose across the forest, reveal the canopy cutaway, and let the island bend and breathe with the wave.
A legend on your leash shows three buff icons beside its sigil, as it gives three times the buff
Every leashed adult now shows its buff icon: gold when it's giving the buff, blue when another of its kind already is, and twinkling pink when it needs feeding

Legends walk round lakes: a happy legend following the ley line, one walking home to sleep, and a charger walking back after its charge all go round the shore instead of getting stuck at the water's edge.
The loading screen now fades out slowly onto her bedroom (about 2.5 seconds; a slider on the pause page), with her alarm going off as the room appears
On a fresh game the witch is in her nightie in bed from the moment the loading screen ends, no longer in her day clothes for a second or two first.
Removed the "too heavy to fly with" message that showed the first time an adult or legend held you on the ground
The note that a link opens a different night from your saved one now fades after 12 seconds, and every save note has a × to close it

Starting the party is a proper spectacle now: a tall column of light shoots up above the treetops, a glowing dome blooms round the decks, bigger and brighter amber and rose sparkles fly out, and it all shows over the treehouse instead of hiding under it.
Once the party's going, press E (square on a controller) at your decks to play the party-start show again. The DJ shouts "make some noise!!!"
Every piece of the party-start show has its own sliders and switches in the pause page, under Party start.
Footpaths now link every area's stump to the stumps of all the areas next to it (and to the dancefloor), going round lakes; no trees grow on them
Footpaths have long straight stretches and gentle curves instead of zig-zags
Tonight's find is in an area of its own (never next to home), at its middle on a little clearing, where the paths lead; that area has no stump and no creatures
Stumps are never closer than 40 m to each other
Footpaths come in several looks each (worn or rutted dirt, laid or sunken flagstones, setts or river cobbles, sound or gappy boardwalks and more), so neighbouring paths look different
Paths have bump maps: stones, cobbles, planks and roots stand out, lit on the side facing the moon or your glow (a slider on the pause page under Paths)
Animal tracks, magic trails and stepping stones are easier to see at night, and root paths no longer look striped
Pause settings stay together on the left, with gold scrollbars at the outer edges of both panes.
Sailing from the sea chart, the map's sea now fades into the island's own sea, the same blue, instead of into a black screen, and you see the sea, the beach and the forest the whole way in
Sailing in, the world curves away below the horizon and the great oak's crown rises over it as you fly in, instead of the camera swinging round to the tree
Pause page: three sliders for the dive's curve (how strong, how fast it grows, how fast it eases off)

After sailing to an island, and after sleeping in the bed, the witch is in her nightie in bed from the first moment you see her, no longer in last night's clothes; her nightie is drawn once and kept, so it's ready every morning
Landing in the bedroom after a sail, the camera no longer jumps as the flight ends: it comes down on her in bed and stays there

Sailing from the sea chart, the island starts being made as soon as you choose it, and the flight in starts as soon as its map is ready, showing the island as it's built, with mist over what isn't yet, instead of a blue screen and then a cut to the bed
The night's tempo stays the same from wave to wave: your record's BPM (120 with none), so the spark keeps one speed all night
Only being knocked down speeds the beat up now; the music's style still changes every wave
Music Lab: the tempo ramp knob is gone, and the style shows one BPM for every wave
A dropped telephone connection keeps your visit while it tries to reconnect.
Reconnecting a call gives slow connections time to respond.
Telephone calls now use the dedicated Witch server.
Calls check the connection again after a pause in the game.
Your trail now follows the path of your dodges exactly, corners and all: dodge in a ^ and the trail draws the ^.

Taking off from the treehouse no longer lands you straight back on the next branch: for 3 seconds after leaving a treehouse floor you fly on over its floors, and for 3 seconds after landing you can't take off or step off again
The treehouse is one open home: Bedrooms 2 and 3 are open to walk into (their furniture still under dust sheets), and the canopy indoors opens in a circle round you.
The cauldron's smoke now spreads 10 m round the pot for about ten seconds, and anyone who walks into it takes the potion.
Stepping off the treehouse with your broom now takes off straight from the floor: no more dropping down and rising again, and the camera stays steady as you fly away.
After a lost party, a creature no longer walks on the spot by its bed.
The challenge circle now sits out on the island's edge, in its far half from home, and the ley line goes round it instead of running over it
The challenge circle's animals stand as grey stone statues by their columns until you step onto its stone floor
Step in and they glow red for four bars, then wake as a wild pack on the beat
Once awake they chase you anywhere; fly off over the treetops outside the challenge area, or get knocked down, and the ones you haven't won go back to their posts as stone, fully healed
The challenge circle's carved sigil follows the fight: faint moonlight while the statues sleep, red as they wake, cold blue in the fight, warm once they're all won
The challenge circle's stone floor catches a little more moonlight, so you can see it before you step in
Animals you've won over wander their area out of the way of your fights until the spell is cast
The music spell's analyser fills the whole challenge circle as you cast it
A creature parked at a sigil outside home now guards as far as its chain reaches (80 m), not 40 m.
A creature parked in the home area, or waiting there while you're in the treehouse, now roams the whole home area instead of standing by its sigil, and still defends it.
Visiting a friend's island no longer rebuilds its beach for every game and music update.
Home starts smaller: 5 areas of home's animals, a different five each night, and one legend that leads to a new island
Home grows by an area for every island you find, up to all 64, with a legend for every 5 areas as on other islands, one of them always leading to a phase-1 island you haven't found while there is one
No find and no challenge circle at home until you've found every island; then home's challenge holds all 128 animals
The treehouse's rooms and furniture are made while the loading screen is up, so they're all there when you wake, with no wait the first time you walk round the house
Smoother frames when no spell is leaving marks on the ground.
The legend circle's words are rewritten.
A legend's circle is always in its own legend area: two legend areas no longer share one area, so a circle no longer turns up in the wrong one.
Stumps, legend circles, the challenge circle and home now keep at least 50 m apart, and 10 m from any lake: stumps no longer crowd each other or stand in the water.
Areas are bigger (about 196 m across, not 168) to make room, so islands are about a sixth larger and the sea chart with them.
Where an area is too small for its legend's circle, the area now grows to hold it at its full size, rather than squeezing the circle up against a stump or the treehouse or shrinking it.
Creatures and legends heading across a lake no longer get stuck turning back and forth at its shore, and the beach witches always sit on sand with room for their campfire.
Islands grow by five areas a phase: 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 (they were 10 to 50), so later nights are shorter
Packs grow with the island's phase: a phase 5 island's last stump has full packs, a phase 1 island's a fifth of the way there
Home's packs grow as you find islands, reaching full packs once every island is found
A kind's island has more kinds of creature and fewer repeats: each other kind lives in one area while kinds from its own side of the compass last, and gets a second only after.
The challenge circle is bigger, and its statues stand further apart: each young statue stands nearer the middle than its adult, mostly in view instead of hidden behind it.
The sigils on the challenge circle's columns float clear above the columns' tops instead of sinking into them.
A new loading screen: the World Tree as a Celtic knot in stars, with COVEN and RUSH in its rings.

Animals keep their ordinary faces for now: no angry, happy or dazed faces, and no open jaw when they bite or yawn. Their moods still show as before: an enraged one's red tint, red eyes and 💢, party clothes and sparkles, stars when stunned.
Soundsystems throw coloured spokes of light that turn with the beat. A slider on the pause page sets their strength.
The treehouse's plants, candles, rugs and other bits stay put on the floor as you walk about
She's in her bed from the first moment you see her: no more appearing outside the treehouse and sliding into bed as the loading screen fades, and the camera stays still.
Sleeping in the bed, she's tucked in as the room goes dark, and the room no longer jumps as she wakes up the next night.
The whole island is ready when the loading screen ends: no trees or creatures popping in, and no pause the first time you reach the beach.
Loading takes longer the first time you visit an island while all of it is drawn; after that it's quick.
Twice as many berry patches in every area
Berry patches are spread evenly through each area's woods instead of bunching together
Berry bushes and mushrooms no longer grow in a stump's fighting ground: they keep about 55 m from every stump
Mushrooms no longer grow beside berry bushes or on paths, unless there's nowhere else in the area
Sailing hands over to the dive sooner, especially to big islands: the grass is grown during the dive instead of before it.

During the dive the island loads in a better order: the house, the coast's sand and waves, the trees you can see most of, the stumps and campfires, then the animals; the beach's shells and starfish come last.
Each area's mist now waits until its trees, stumps, campfires and animals are actually drawn, then fades away over a few seconds instead of vanishing.
The dive flies higher over the island, in a darker, hazier light that eases back to the night's as you land.
The zoom into the sea chart and the dive onto the island can no longer be skipped: they're the island loading.
Changed your mind? E or the pad's circle during the first moments of the zoom puts the chart down and stops the sail; you stay on the same night at the map table.
Sailing from the map table zooms into the sea chart again: holding the key, button or mouse to sail no longer skipped the zoom straight to a blue screen.
In bed she sits up on the mattress, facing the foot of the bed, instead of standing in the middle of it; her stretch as she gets up is in bed too
In bed the duvet covers her legs, in the bed's own colours
In bed her nightie no longer glows to a white blob: her own glow and the bloom are softened until she's up
Take your broom for the night from the new broom rack
Your broom is modded at three stations: tips at the new workbench, the body at the lathe, exhausts at the new hydraulic lift
The broom stations only light up while you're carrying your broom, and show it on the vice, lathe or lift
Each broom station fits on the screen, with your sets and your broom's stats at the bottom
The pegboard is now just for show: your finds hang on it
The hydraulic lift hisses up and down
The coloured spokes of light round the playing soundsystems now visibly turn, once every 2 bars and faster as the tempo rises, on up to three nearby stumps instead of only the nearest

The dressing table's skin colours are now a full range of human skin tones (the Monk Skin Tone Scale), palest to deepest, plus five witchy tones: frost blue, lilac, ash grey, moss green and night indigo
Random witches and Randomise now pick from the full range of human skin tones
A new witch's starting skin is now the nearest tone on the new range
The skin colour you choose now stays the same after reloading the game
Every treehouse station menu now fits on the screen: no more scrolling
New basin by the bed: skin tone, makeup (lipstick, eyeshadow, blush) and a button to brush your teeth
Each station holds fewer things: hair, sunglasses and earrings at the dressing table; jacket and top on the wardrobe rail; trousers and shoes at the shoe rack
Bags show as small cards; the one you're on shows how it throws, with its firing preview
Smaller colour swatches, and what you're wearing is clearly marked, even on pale colours
Things you haven't found yet show as grey shapes, no padlocks
Menus open on what you're wearing, and the camera frames the part of you each station changes
Guest bedrooms get their own basin and shoe rack
The DJ booth matches the other menus, and its prompt hides while it's open
Your first morning starts at the basin, then the dressing table
A new witch starts with light green skin

The pause page's Tree normal maps test switch is now a choice: full, 64, 32 or 16 directions, or off. The reduced ones cut each tree atlas's normal map to that many directions, to judge how few the trees can keep and still look right. Full stays the default.
A test switch on the pause page turns the trees' normal maps off, so the trees are lit flat, to judge whether they still look right without them. Normal maps stay on by default.
A new singer: the voice in the breakdowns and builds now sings with Chimera's voice, a note made for every pitch it sings, on "ah" and "ooh", so every note is in tune
To compare with the old singer, add ?singer=recorded to the link; the Music Lab's voice choice has both

The quiet stretches of the music are haunted: the singer floats in a long, dark reverb over a slow drone, holding her notes, with a ghostly second voice a sixth below her and darker notes at the ends of phrases
Each quiet stretch then drops into drum & bass
A sleeping legend's clearing has the same dark reverb, drone and ghostly echo, and no drums
The melodies dance: the lead plays a catchy riff that repeats every bar and answers itself every fourth, in the styles of trance, hip-hop, witch house and bright electro-pop

Twelve new lead sounds to play them on: trance supersaws, plucks and stabs, a dusty electric piano, lo-fi keys and a breathy flute, a dark saw, a music box and a low choir, bright arpeggio synths, glassy bells and an airy synth voice
The singer sometimes sings a short, high hook over and over, and in the haunted breakdowns she sings the tune slowly before the drop plays it as a riff
The basslines step into each chord change, change over four bars, lock in with the kick drum and slide between notes in the hip-hop and witch-house styles
The house bass sits lower and rounder, moves smoothly from chord to chord, leaves the kick drum room, and changes its rhythm every few bars instead of bouncing on every offbeat
Creatures' spells glow: a bright core with a pixel halo, a pool of light on the ground under each shot, hit and zone, and the brightest few light the forest around them
Legends' blows and party animals' spells glow too, in their own colours; Reduce flashing halves the glow
Your 💌 invitations fly faster and further (45 m/s for 42 m, up from 31.2 m/s for 33 m) and home in from further off, so they catch running animals
Animals waiting in a fight keep the same distance as before, so the longer throws now reach them
To compare with the old invitations, add ?invites=old to the link

A new music mode, on by default: every night has one catchy hook that returns at the big moments (each wave landing, the drum & bass drop after a breakdown, the victory), with each wave's own riff in between
The night starts gentle and opens up into the full rave once the second stump has its soundsystem
Each genre has its own drum kit and groove, with fills, crashes and swing; builds strip the bass and kick away and leave a beat of silence before the drop
The singer sings the hook slowly in the breakdowns, and a sleeping legend's clearing hums it
A brighter, punchier mix, with a clean sub under the bass
The old music is one switch away with ?banger=0
Compressors on the drums and on the whole mix, for punch and to glue it together
A kick drum with more thump, and the bass ducking out of its way
Square-wave leads as the main sound, with a little pulse-wave reply; a few genres keep their own instruments
The singer doubles the hook when it lands, holds soft oohs under the grooves and adds sung stabs
The lead melodies sit lower and quieter, in the groove with the drums
A xylophone and finger snaps drift in and out for a spookier feel
The music now asks much less of your computer while you play, which should stop it crunching and cutting out on some laptops; it sounds the same
More space in the music: fewer parts playing at once in the grooves, a bigger reverb with crisp hits, and echoes that bounce left and right
The xylophone now plays chords and arpeggios in many genres, with a darker, lower one in the gentle start
The singer sings three-part harmonies under the grooves
Claps and finger snaps on the backbeat instead of a snare drum in most genres
Drums and bass sit bigger in the mix, and the whole thing is wider
The xylophone and finger snaps are now loud enough to hear
Basslines sit lower and deeper
Finger snaps and claps now take turns: snaps in the lighter stretches, claps when the music is full
The singer sings higher and brighter, the kick drum is deeper, and the xylophone and chords sit lower
The music leans more minor, with a darker turn at the end of each chord loop
Much less shaker
The singer now lands exactly with the lead melody instead of a touch late
New melodies: long held notes joined by quick runs and turns, over a rolling xylophone pattern
House sections get a bouncy two-bar riff played by the lead, xylophone and singer together, which builds each time it comes round
Breakdowns are dreamier and quieter, with stacked voices; breakbeat sections and drum & bass drops hit harder, with a gritty bass
The singer harmonises the hook when it lands
Some house riffs are now a simple chant on a three-three-two rhythm, with the singer on every note
The singer now leads: she sings the main tune herself in most styles, with the synth supporting underneath
Her voice is lighter and brighter, with a wide, dreamy echo around the long notes
The kick drum hits harder
Walking north or south, grass, flowers and trees no longer flicker a pixel back and forth
Which of two overlapping things is drawn on top no longer depends on where the camera is
Putting on a jacket or top at the wardrobe no longer puts your trousers on too: trousers go on at the shoe rack, and until then her nightie shows under the jacket
With her trousers on but not her top, she wears her nightie over her jeans
The challenge circle stays hidden in the forest until the party starts, then fades in as its trees fade away; if it isn't won, it fades back into forest when the party's over

When you start the party at your decks, the burst of sparkles, the pillar of light and the dome are gone: a rainbow audio analyser ring, like the soundsystem spell's, now spreads across the Terrace's floor around the decks, moves with the music, and fades a bar after the music drops

The analyser ring at your decks now reads as separate bars that rise and fall with the music, jump with each scratch of your needle-drop routine before the music starts, and stay on the Terrace's floor instead of hanging over its edge
Sleeping legends now lie at the back of their circles, leaving room at the front to stand before them; the circles are a little bigger to make space
Standing at the middle of a legend circle, you are now in view in front of the sleeping legend: the elephant, mole and bear included
Makeup at the basin is now one colour for your lips and eyes together: pick a colour to put it on, pick the same colour again to take it off
Blush is gone; if you were wearing it, it comes off
Home's animals are redrawn as low-poly models on skeletons: fox, stoat, hare, squirrel, dormouse, badger, mole, hedgehog and snail, each with its own baby, young, adult and legend
A giant bee now lives in the old pinewood in the marten's place: it flies, and stings from range
A turtle now lives in the Fen in the newt's place: slow and armoured, it spits a jet of pond water, and sleeps in its shell
They walk on eight frames instead of two, and legends wear plate armour cut with glowing runes
Asleep they lie down; sleeping legends curl up in a ring, nose to tail, and the snail draws into its shell

They stand on the ground now instead of floating over it, and stride properly: the fox trots, the hare, stoat, squirrel and dormouse bound, the badger, mole and hedgehog trot low, and each stands still on all its feet when it stops
The treehouse's stations have new places: the basin, telescope, broom rack, hydraulic lift and workbench among them
The animals' feet now stay planted as they walk and run instead of sliding: each has a slow walk and a proper run, and picks between them by how fast it's going
Their bodies move as they go: they bob, sway and roll, bounders stretch out and gather, heads stay steady and tails follow
The mole's great hands paddle in time with its steps, and the baby bee no longer dips to the ground
Creatures' shots now aim where you're going: keep changing direction to dodge
Shots fly faster, and a creature stands still for a moment before it lets go
Tigers' and cats' adult claws, and young rhinos' logs, no longer leave a safe gap right where you stand
Taking off from the treehouse should no longer freeze, after a sail or not: the house seen from the air and your sigil stack are now prepared ahead
A quick tap of the sigil button now puts down or picks up exactly one sigil; hold it a moment to start a run
Sigils flash in their own colour as they fly between the ground and her head, burn into the ground with a glow when put down, and sparkle above her head when picked up
Going to sleep at the bed now closes her eyes: the screen darkens from the edges as you hold, and opens again if you let go early
Waking up in the morning, her eyes open the same way
At the dressing stations, the None and Bare cards now show her without it (no sunglasses, bare ears, no cloak, no scarf), and the Trainers card shows her trainers, instead of a ∅
At the Workshop, a broom slot's empty card shows the plain broom there: the handle's bare end, the plain handle, or her straw bristles
Challenge statues stand closer together: the elder 10 m in from its column, the youth 10 m further.
Up in the treetops, pulling against a creature's chain drags you down: a short tug dips you and you rise again; keep pulling and you come down to the ground
On the ground, pulling a creature's chain slows you much less, and the creature hurries after you
Keep pulling on the ground and you'll see that creature's sigil slide out of your stack; ease off and it slides back, keep going and it drops where you are
A legend's chain yanks you back instead
Adult chains are bigger than young ones, and legend chains bigger still
Chains are a softer silvery violet, with a flash of the creature's colour running along them now and then

The forest through the telescope is all there the moment you look, in every direction, from the first look of the night; on a slow machine what is still on its way is covered in mist that rolls back as it arrives
Walking between the treehouse terrace and its rooms no longer swings the camera or changes the light: the house is one place now
Trees are shaded from a smaller set of light directions (32), close to before but lighter to draw.
The game no longer waits for the trees' shading to be worked out: trees start with their full shading and switch a moment after load.
New Wild look group on the pause page: her light's reach, brightness and colour in the wild, and a new colour grade that only shows in the wild (off at first)
The swallowtail butterfly is its own animal in the game's files now, no longer filed under the moth's name: nothing about it changes, and islands you found or won as the moth's are still yours
The moth is a moth again, furry with feathery feelers and dusky wings, waiting on the bench: it has no island yet
Her line of babies is spaced by how long each one is now drawn, so they no longer walk through each other: long ones like otters, hares and tigers keep further apart
The stones round the dancefloor are low, rounded boulders now, about knee height and no two alike, so they no longer look like the speakers they turn into
The ring of bars round the decks at the party start is now a full circle: its bars carry on past the edge of the Terrace instead of stopping at it
The soundsystem spell's ring of bars at a great stump is even north and south: the bass now plays at both, so the north bars are no longer the short ones
The grass at the edge of her light no longer shimmers as she walks: its fade stays put on each tuft
On a slower machine, far trees and decor fade out and back in gently instead of popping when the frame rate dips
String lights at the far edge go out bulb by bulb, not a whole string at once

Your own magic glows like the creatures' spells: the party start's bars at the decks, your blink and the ley line's spark each get a bright core, a pixel halo and a pool of light on the ground, and light the forest around them
A pool of light follows you on the ground as you fly, in your trail's colour; Reduce flashing halves the glow
A friendly legend with nothing to fight now walks the whole of tonight's route to its far end, turns round and walks back, then stays to guard the home area alongside the island's own home legend
Creatures' lunges are much longer: they wind up from about a dash and a half away, then lunge about two dashes, straight through and past where you were. Dash sideways out of the line.

The wolf, arctic fox, fennec, raccoon, red panda, otter and meerkat are now drawn as low-poly models, like home's creatures: they plant their feet, trot or bound, and their legends wear armour with glowing runes
The cats are redrawn as low-poly models on skeletons: sand cat, lynx, cheetah, lion, tiger, black jaguar and snow leopard, each with its own baby, young, adult and legend, at the sizes they were
The sand cat, lynx, cheetah and snow leopard bound at speed; the lion, tiger and jaguar trot; all of them curl up nose to tail to sleep
Their legends wear plate armour cut with glowing runes: the lion's mane is flame, the snow leopard carries its tail over its back, the cheetah trails streamers
The hoofed animals are redrawn as low-poly models on skeletons: stag, elk, roe deer, ram, ibex and boar, each with its own baby, young, adult and legend, at the sizes they were
They have cloven hooves, and antlers, horns and tusks that grow with them: a fawn has none, a legend's are vast, mossy or banded, with lit points
The stag, elk, ram and boar trot; the roe deer and the ibex spring along stiff-legged at speed
Asleep, deer, sheep and goats fold their forelegs under them; their legends curl up on their sides in plate armour cut with glowing runes

The bear, polar bear, rhino, elephant, beaver and flying squirrel are new low-poly models: they stride with planted feet, the elephant has a trunk that swings and ears like sails, the rhino's horn grows as it does, the beaver has its paddle of a tail and the flying squirrel its glide skin. Their legends wear rune-lit armour.

The cold-blooded animals are redrawn as low-poly models on skeletons: salamander, Komodo dragon, crocodile, toad, armadillo, jungle python and rattlesnake, each with its own baby, young, adult and legend, at the sizes they were
The snakes slither: their curves stay put on the ground as they pass through them, and they coil up to sleep with their heads on top
The salamander, Komodo dragon and crocodile walk sprawled, legs out to their sides and their backs swinging; the toad hops; the armadillo scurries under a banded shell

Their legends wear plate armour cut with glowing runes: a salamander crested with flame, a mossed stone Komodo, a crocodile with standing stones down its back, a hooded python, a horned rattlesnake with a great rattle

The winged animals are redrawn as low-poly models on skeletons: heron, raven, spotted owl, penguin, swallowtail, fruit bat and dragonfly, each with its own baby, young, adult and legend, at the sizes they were
The heron and the raven walk, the owl hops, and all three take off and fly low when they go fast, wings beating; the penguin waddles, quicker in a hurry
The swallowtail, the fruit bat and the dragonfly fly at every pace on their own wings: slow painted ones, skin between long fingers, four of glass

Asleep, the raven tucks its bill into its back, the heron hunches on its feet, the owl sits with its eyes shut, the penguin lies on its front, the butterfly shuts its wings upright and the bat wraps itself in its own

Their legends wear plate armour cut with glowing runes: a lamp-billed heron, a gold-hoarding raven, an owl ringed with lit eyes, an ice-plated emperor penguin, a swallowtail with two great eyes on its wings, a great-eared bat with lit fingers, a giant tattered dragonfly
The many-legged animals are redrawn as low-poly models on skeletons: fire beetle, woodlouse, tarantula, scorpion and crab, each with its own baby, young, adult and legend, at the sizes they were
They walk on all their legs with their feet planted: the beetle's six go as two tripods, the tarantula's, scorpion's and crab's eight as two fours, and the woodlouse's fourteen in a ripple
The crab scuttles sideways, facing you as it passes, and waves its great claw
The woodlouse rolls into a ball to sleep; the scorpion lays its tail round its side; the others fold their legs in

Their legends wear plate armour cut with glowing runes: a beetle with burning antlers, a fortress of a woodlouse, a tarantula plated in rose glass, a scorpion elder carrying its young, a crab with one colossal claw
The griffin, sphinx, unicorn, frost wyrm, frost troll, hydra, feathered serpent and stegosaurus are redrawn as low-poly models, like the rest
The hydra's heads now take turns to spit: left, middle, right

Wild creatures' shots now mark the ground where they land: a brief scorch, frost patch, splash or patch of rough ground in the shot's element. Stand in one for a moment and it hurts or slows you (?shotmarks=0 turns them off, to compare)
